slides.headline: Neutral spine isn't a pose to hold
slides.sub: What your Pilates instructor actually means, and why it isn't rigid.

slides.title: It's a range, not a point
slides.body: Neutral spine is simply a position where your spine's natural curves are present, not flattened or exaggerated. It differs between people, and there's a comfortable zone rather than one exact spot.

slides.title: Why we use it in Pilates
slides.body: Starting from neutral gives you a consistent reference, so you can feel what your trunk, hips and shoulders are doing. It's a teaching tool for control, not a rule for everyday life.

slides.title: What it doesn't mean
slides.body: It doesn't mean your spine should never bend or twist. Healthy backs flex, round and rotate all day long. Plenty of Pilates exercises deliberately move you out of neutral, and that's the point.

slides.title: Find yours in 30 seconds
slides.body: Lie on your back with knees bent. Gently tip your pelvis to flatten your lower back, then arch it. Settle about halfway, with a small gap under your lower back. That's roughly neutral.

slides.title: Easy on the bracing
slides.body: Holding neutral shouldn't mean clenching your stomach and holding your breath. Light, steady effort and relaxed breathing usually work better and make the exercises feel smoother.

slides.headline: Curious what neutral feels like?
slides.body: Our clinical Pilates team at Hybrid Physiotherapy starts with an assessment and coaches you through it on the mat or reformer. Book online, link in bio.

caption:
"Find your neutral spine." If that cue leaves you frozen and unsure, you're in good company.

Neutral simply means your spine's natural curves are there, not flattened or exaggerated. It's a comfortable zone rather than one perfect position, and it looks a little different on everyone.

In Pilates it's a reference point for control, not a rule that your back should never bend. Healthy spines round, arch and twist all day, and many exercises move you out of neutral on purpose. Light effort and easy breathing beat bracing hard.
